subject: Runway ops walkthrough & temporary standby activation for EchoWave deal
messages:
From: Nina Shah <nina@echowave.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@echowave.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Late-stage capacity request — temporary standby for ramp week

Hi Tessa,

We're getting close to commit review with the board (target next Tues). The legal and procurement teams want a short formal note that Redwood can hold a temporary standby of GPU capacity for the expected ramp week (estimated 72 hours) immediately after go-live.

Quick stats from our side (attached):
- Peak concurrent inference workers: 48
- Typical sequence length: 1.2k tokens
- Expected qps during ramp: 120 sustained, bursts to 240
- Preferred instance class: A100-like / 80GB equivalence

Can you confirm whether a soft hold is possible, what the activation lead time would be, and an estimated cost delta for a 72-hour standby? If you need more technical detail, looping in our infra lead.

Thanks,
Nina Shah
Head of Product
EchoWave AI

Attachment: EchoWave_workload_profile_v1.csv (see included per-request load profile)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Nina Shah <nina@echowave.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Late-stage capacity request — temporary standby for ramp week

Nina — thanks for the profile and the clear numbers. Congrats on the board milestone.

Short answers up front:
- We can provision a temporary standby (soft hold) against the Dedicated pool for a 72-hour activation window.
- Activation lead time: 24–36 hours for full A100-equivalent capacity in our us-west region (we can do faster but would require approval for burst slots).
- Cost delta: I'll get engineering to size and confirm a precise cost; rough ballpark is ~1.6x runtime cost for fully reserved 72h standby vs on-demand.

Karthik / Ben — can you run a quick sizing check against the attached workload and confirm SKU mix and whether we should stage any lower-memory quantized variants as fallback? Please include: expected node count, thermal bin considerations, and an ops play for automated fallback to L4-quantized replicas if memory pressure shows up.

I attached the SOW draft that procurement requested — it's preliminary but includes the activation window clause. Procurement (cc) may want that in the response for legal.

Next step: Karthik, Ben — can you reply within EOD with a recommendation and cost-range? I want to send a concise note back to procurement tonight so EchoWave can present to the board tomorrow.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_EchoWave_v0.9.pdf (draft)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Late-stage capacity request — temporary standby for ramp week

Team — did a rapid pass on the attached CSV and the metrics Nina listed. Notes below.

Sizing summary (recommended):
- Target SKU: 80GB A100-equivalent nodes (we'll map to our Dedicated pod type: dGPU-80x).
- Node count: 12 nodes (each node can sustain ~20 qps at 1.2k sequence with our current kernel selection + batching heuristics) => ~240 qps burst headroom. For sustained 120 qps, 6 nodes should be enough; recommending 12 to meet burst and buffer.
- KV cache sizing: prewarm 60% keyspace before ramp to reduce cold-start overhead.
- Thermal bin: prefer bin-2 mapped racks; avoid bin-4 racks during sustained 72h run to mitigate throttling risk. Ops: reserve nodes across 3 racks to limit blast radius.

Fallbacks / quantization options:
- L4x quantized model variants available; switching reduces memory usage by ~30% and increases per-node qps by ~10% at cost of a small quality delta. We can stage 12 L4x replicas as cold standby to flip if memory/thermal alarms trigger.

Lead times and activations:
- Soft hold (reservation) for 72h standby: can be committed within 24 hours. Activation plan: 1) place soft hold, 2) prewarm KV caches 12 hours before window, 3) health-check and smoke test 1 hour prior, 4) open traffic via routing policy.

Estimated cost delta (very rough):
- Reserved standby 72h on Dedicated dGPU-80x: $79,500 ± 8% (this includes prewarming and support shifts)
- On-demand alternative (no hold): $46,000 ± 10% (higher chance of capacity unavailability during burst)

Dev — can you confirm the prewarm script and whether 12 nodes is safe w.r.t our current autoscaler thresholds? Also note any additional logging/trace flags procurement may ask for.

-Karthik

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Late-stage capacity request — temporary standby for ramp week

Agree with Karthik's sizing. Ops notes:
- We'll reserve nodes across 3 physical racks in us-west-2 (bin-2 preferred).
- Proposed runbook steps attached inline below.

Runbook (high level):
1) Approve soft hold and mark nodes Q:reserve in the scheduler.
2) Stage model variants (standard + L4x) in the model registry as tags: echo_standard, echo_l4x_cold.
3) Start KV prewarm 12h prior; monitor 95th pct latency and cache hit-rate.
4) 1h prior smoke test at 10% traffic.
5) At ramp, enable routing policy with gradual traffic shift over 12 minutes.
6) If thermal alarms > 75% in any rack -> trigger automated routing to L4x replicas and notify on-call.

I'll prepare the compact note for procurement with cost bullets and the runbook. If procurement needs SLAs for that 72h window, we'll offer a one-time SLA addendum (standard enterprise process).

-Ben

Attachment: ops_runbook_compact.txt (text)

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Nina Shah <nina@echowave.ai>, procurement@echowave.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Late-stage capacity request — temporary standby for ramp week

Thanks — quick engineering confirmation and a small ops caveat.

Confirmations:
- Prewarm script: yes, we have a prewarm job that will warm both weights cache and KV entries; script takes ~6–10 minutes per node (we recommend parallel execution across nodes).
- Autoscaler: set to honor a hard ceiling at 16 nodes for this customer ID to avoid noisy neighbor impacts. With 12 nodes reserved we're within safe thresholds.
- Logging: we'll enable token-level sampling at 0.1% and full request traces for 1% of traffic during ramp; we'll deliver audit logs post-window.

Caveat: if Echowave's production traffic includes long chained streaming calls (multiple partial generations per request), per-node qps will dip ~12–18% vs the batch-model used in the CSV. Please confirm if the 120/240 qps figures are per-inference call or per-token streaming sessions.

Action items:
- Nina / EchoWave: confirm whether 120/240 qps numbers are per-inference-call. If yes, we are green to proceed.
- Tessa: I'll prepare a compact procurement note that includes the activation timeline, cost range, and the runbook excerpt. I'll also attach the prewarm checksum and script name.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops_runbook_compact.txt (text)
Attachment: prewarm_script_checksum.txt (text)
